control: Same identity-source.png and cat.png; replaced exactly one style paragraph of the previous prompt. Stochastic model/version effects are uncontrolled.
comparison_method: Manual visual inspection at native output view against original isolated photo, cat.png and old P03; no calibrated identity/style score.

findings.observation: Some dark torso and forehead regions have larger calmer planes than the old P03. Orange body areas still contain many small fragmented facets.
Visible white whiskers and hair-like streaks appeared around muzzle and white bib despite explicit no-hair constraints. The chest also has thin radiating facets.

Right orange/left black cheek asymmetry, dark nasal bridge, small pink nose, white bib/paws and yellow-green eyes remain broadly recognizable. Exact patch boundaries were simplified and have not passed quantitative or multi-view validation.
Lying pose, source-visible paws and left clipped tail remain; no exact silhouette/landmark preservation claim.
No new mesh, UV, rig or animation was generated. Current 3500-triangle model is unchanged.

system_learning: Prompt-only facet-size control did not reliably enforce the no-hair/clean-facet specification in this one trial. A successful isolated region does not justify adding this as a mandatory production step.
not_proven: That the changed paragraph alone caused every observed difference
A generally reliable automatic style scorer
Improved true 3D output from this reference
stop_condition_reached: One allowed image generated and reviewed; no repeat image edits or downstream Tripo request.
next_required_work: Separate reference-image style and identity requirements from actual mesh/material acceptance; next experiment must test a shared rule with a defined quality check, rather than keep adjusting this cat by hand.
